brief: A seed-starting tray of at least four cells, each with a draining bin.

requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray of at least four cells
requirements.evidence: Four full-depth base pieces in a hex cluster at cells (0,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (1,0) on level 0, joined with joint bolts (lockJoints) and open faces capped (capOpenFaces). check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Each of the four cells holds a hex-bin-full-drain (full depth, drained) bin: bin:0,0,0, bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:1,0,0. Each was filled with soil and planted with a seedling prop.

finish.summary: Built a four-cell seed-starting tray: four connected full-depth bases, each carrying a drained full-depth bin, locked with joint bolts and capped at open faces. The bins are filled with soil and seedling props for staging. Clean check: no rule issues, meshes clear. Drainage is the bin's drilled floor shape only; I cannot verify materials or water-tightness of the print.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
